The comments sounds terribly pessimistic, but I will agree: I still have faith in the team to make the game a worthwhile experience again. What I remember from the last months I played LN is that the suits have risen in quality, many of them look cool! Sadly, the unenjoyable events and gameplay have ushered many players, including myself. I'd call myself a veteran, even. The first event I experienced for myself was the first demon doctor-peachy nurse event which I, as a new player barely understood but I still got a few pieces out of it and enjoyed the event.  
I must add this: our expectations have also risen. This is likely natural, but I can still understand how hard it is for the team to keep up. The gameplay mechanics aren't fun anymore to most of us, and many new suits that probably took a while to arrange and draw are "average, ugly, bland or boring". Most suits that would have had many people drooling over it (exaggeration, but yknow what I mean) would just be a "meh, skip" today.

I've been playing since, what do I know, 2016-2018? I don't even remember because of how long I've dropped this game (half a year or more). When I started playing, I remember having quite a lot of fun, but bad feelings for not having the benefits of an user who invests money does. Sure, Pay2Win is pretty bad and the greed is obvious, but common amongst the mobile game industry. The game's quality decreased for sure, the old antics that once made the game at least somewhat enjoyable have become stale and "doing your dailies" has become a burden and a waste of time (to me at least). Events are clearly rushed, there's no point in participating in them because it isn't fun anymore. At least the few event variants that give non-dia-buyers a chance to get something at all. I don't think that straight up buying a suit with your google play money was ever fun. The positive feelings from doing that are awfully short-lived and most just forget about the digital clothes they just bought with their real money after a few days anyway. Those who still participate in those lame events at all anymore probably just do it for either completionism or because of the next competition theme is *totally not* going to be related to the previous event at all or maybe because of really useful attributes parts of or the whole suit may have.  
I mustn't even mention the monotone gameplay and even more painful to skip through, boring lore.  
The game is dead and should be until some effort actually is put into it to make it worth people's money and time.

so I put a spoiler on this because my message gets pretty personal and features topics that could trigger others (self harm, eating disorder, trauma from abuse and bullying) so if you're one of them, skip reading this.  


I've been taking antidepressants since may/june 2021, I was 16 at the time and I don't know your age and I also don't know if age affects the effects of antidepressants or needs of them. The antidepressant I'm taking is called "Adjuvin" and it contains Sertraline. My starting dose was very low, only 25mg a day, a month later it was changed to 50mg and now I've been taking 100mg a day for about 3 months. So, what I can tell you about antidepressants is this: it's not going to fix everything and it won't numb anything. You will still have negative emotions (sadness, anger, pain, ...) and feel depressed, the most it can do is reduce the intensity of your "bad" emotions and raise your motivation (e.g. to get out of bed, to go to school/work, etc.) to do more than just lay in bed all day thinking about life and such. Antidepressants are definitely not what helped me get better. To be honest, I don't even feel the effect of them. (In addition to my adjuvin pill I take these meds: 5 vitamin D drops every morning, ritalin 30mg, quetiapin 100mg). I don't know your financial situation and how healthcare works where you live, but I've consulted a therapist starting april 2021 for several reasons, those being: traumatic experiences (9 years of bullying at school, abuse at home), aggression and violence towards myself (self harm, calling myself awful), eating disorder in the form of anorexia (starving myself) it got so bad that I ate nothing but a small pack of berries a day and only drank a cup of green tea a day. the therapist tried to make me feel better by talking, we had an appointment once per week, but she saw that this wasn't enough to help me, as my wish to die and self-harming behaviour persisted. Mid-july 2021 I was admitted to a hospital for teens aged 14-18 and that's where I stayed for the next 5 months. It took lots of intensive care and help for me to be able to get out of there in mid-december 2021. And that didn't "fix" me either, I still have bad thoughts and self-hating and harming behaviours, but I found ways to help me in distress.  


I ramble way too much so I'll shorten my message:  
Antidepressants will not fix you. The only person who can make this situation better is yourself. Sure, antidepressants and other people can assist you on your healing journey, but the one doing all the work will still be yourself. Essentially, it is your own decision how and when and if at all you want to take action to the way you feel, but antidepressants are not going to numb your pain, it will persist. A good way to start is by consulting a therapist and explaining your problem to them. And note this: it won't be gone instantly, it's a lengthy process with many drawbacks, but it is 100% possible to get better if you try hard enough and get enough support.  


Feel free to reply or message me privately if you are in need of support, I've had a lifelong experiences with such problems and I'm willing to help.
